name: Question 10
problem: A pest infestation is spreading through a land with $300$ trees. The rate of growth in the number of trees $P(t)$ infected with the pest is jointly proportional to the number of trees that are infected at time $t,$ measured in months,  and the number of uninfected trees. If the constant of proportionality is $0.2,$ which differential equation could be used to model $P(t)?$

html:
Question 10
?

A pest infestation is spreading through a land with 300 trees. The rate of growth in the number of trees P(t) infected with the pest is jointly proportional to the number of trees that are infected at time t, measured in months, and the number of uninfected trees. If the constant of proportionality is 0.2, which differential equation could be used to model P(t)?

a
dPdt=−0.2P(300−P)
b
dPdt=300P(0.2+P)
c
dPdt=300P(0.2−P)
d
dPdt=0.2P(300−P)
e
dPdt=0.2P(300+P)
